law2Routing.whyFaithfulnessAndNotQA: This is the Law-1-overrides-Law-2 clause made concrete: 'if a story's own intended behaviour would introduce an exploit, flag the unsafe story - do not bless a faithful-but-exploitable implementation.' The implementation of story-003 is FAITHFUL - the story prescribes the defective check verbatim in Technical Details and the executor's only departure (hoisting the sum into a local, Autonomous Decision 3) is behaviour-identical. There is therefore no deviation to report, and grading this run's faithfulness as 'clean' on that basis would be exactly the blessing Law 1 forbids. The unsafe story is the finding, and the spec-conformance report is where a story-level judgement belongs and where the owner will actually read it.

classification.assetImpact: NONE from the document itself. Its consequence is that the defect now filed as M-07 stands ACCEPTED in the story tree on a stated ground the proof refutes, so a future story or triager reading that record will believe the question is settled.
attackPath: 1. story-003 was planned, executed and reviewed inline by one harness. Both the Autonomous Decisions section and the Review Results Executive Summary disclose this loudly and both explicitly ask for a real reviewer: 'The independence this delegation buys is genuinely absent here, so this story's review carries more weight than usual - it should get a real reviewer, not a rubber stamp.'

2. The Auto-Completed section records 'Approved by: story-batch workflow (machine approval - not human-reviewed)'. The request for a real reviewer was therefore never met; it was closed by the machine.

3. That section carries four non-blocking findings forward. Item 2 reads: '[medium] minPhUSDOut == 0 at a zero exchange rate lets the caller surrender the stable half for only the antimatter half. This is the explicitly planned and NatSpec-documented semantics of a waived slippage floor (standard minOut == 0 DeFi behaviour) ... It is a caller-side protection the caller opted out of, not a protocol defect.'

4. THAT IS M-07, and the disposition is wrong on the arithmetic. The record's entire ground is that the caller CHOSE to waive protection by passing zero. Halmos INV-A proves that every minPhUSDOut in [0, amount] is equally inert, so a caller who passes a non-zero floor - who is exercising the protection, not waiving it - lands in the identical outcome. 'Standard minOut == 0 DeFi behaviour' is precisely what this is not: in the standard pattern a non-zero minOut binds.

5. Compounding it, the story's Concerns section pre-committed to the same reasoning ('it waives the caller's own protection rather than exposing the protocol'), and the same harness that wrote that sentence reviewed it and approved it. No independent step existed at which the arithmetic could have been checked.
classification.likelihood: CERTAIN as a documented state - the record exists and says what it says.

law1Override.clause: Law 1 overrides Law 2: a story whose own intended behaviour introduces a defect is flagged as an unsafe story rather than blessed as a faithful implementation.
law1Override.applied: story-003's Technical Details prescribe the inert check verbatim, and its Concerns section pre-approves the semantics that make it inert. The defect is upstream of the executor. This flag is the Law-1 record of that.
law1Override.corroboration: The same pattern appears one layer down in the ledger: F-01's human triageReason sanctioned deleting the protocol-side zero guard on the premise that 'a post-burn revert unwinds the whole transaction anyway' - also refuted by INV-A. The unsafe reasoning was agreed at BOTH the triage and the story layer before any code was written, which is why an independent reviewer was the control that mattered and why its absence is filed rather than noted.

justification: LOW, routed to spec-conformance, and disposable only by a human. The band is honest: a story document is not deployed and puts no asset at risk, so QA/Low is the ceiling and anything higher would be overstatement of a process artifact. What lifts it off the QA floor is that this is not merely 'no independent reviewer' - that alone is a process note. It is that the acceptance record affirmatively DISPOSES of the defect this run files as a Medium, on a stated ground the run's own proof refutes, and it does so in the tree that the next story will read as settled context. That is the false-closure class the pipeline has been bitten by repeatedly, and the fact that the closure was applied by machine approval, over the executor's and reviewer's own written request for a real reviewer, is what removed the step that would have caught it. Two things are deliberately NOT claimed. The work is not accused of infidelity - the implementation matches the story exactly, and saying otherwise would misdirect the fix. And no reward-hacking is alleged: the review re-ran the build and suite, verified each checklist claim against the code, and disclosed its own non-independence prominently in three separate places. The failure is not dishonesty, it is that a self-review cannot catch an error that the story's own reasoning already contains.
recommendation: A HUMAN - not this pipeline and not a future run of it - must revisit story-003's Auto-Completed non-blocking item 2 and record that its ground is refuted: the inertness is not confined to minPhUSDOut == 0 and is not the standard minOut == 0 pattern. Until that is done, the story tree carries an acceptance of M-07 that a later story may reasonably build on.

Re-open the request the story itself made and the batch closed: story-003 should receive a real independent review, because the defect it shipped is upstream of the executor and only an independent step could have caught it.

Treat machine approval as unavailable for a story whose own Review Results ask for a human, and for any story whose carried-forward findings include a [medium]. A [medium] dispositioned non-blocking by the same harness that wrote it is not a triage.
